cards.explanation: The answer is False. The psalm says, "The LORD reigns; let the nations tremble!" (Psalm 99:1). Nobody trembling is also leaning back with their feet up, friends. It's the opposite of a nap. The reign of the LORD gets a big response, and this verse is only the start of it.

The answer is above all the peoples. The psalm says, "Great is the LORD in Zion; He is exalted above all the peoples." (Psalm 99:2). All the peoples is a big circle, friends, and nobody gets left outside it. Zion is where He's called great, and the whole world is under that same word.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "The mighty King loves justice. You have established equity; You have exercised justice and righteousness in Jacob." (Psalm 99:4). Notice it says justice and righteousness together, bakers. I'd keep that pair in my apron pocket.

The answer is Moses and Aaron. The psalm says, "Moses and Aaron were among His priests…" (Psalm 99:6). Notice it says "among" His priests, so the psalm isn't saying they were the only two. Two names, friends, and the psalm is just getting warmed up.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "They called to the LORD and He answered." (Psalm 99:6). That's three names, Moses, Aaron and Samuel, and one clear result. Calling and being answered sit right next to each other in that line.
The answer is kept. The psalm says, "they kept His decrees and the statutes He gave them." (Psalm 99:7). He spoke from the pillar of cloud, and they kept what He gave. Simple as that, friends.

The answer is forgiving yet an avenger of their misdeeds. The psalm says, "You were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their misdeeds." (Psalm 99:8). Both halves are in the same verse, and it keeps both. Don't drop either one, bakers.

The answer is mountain. The psalm ends, "Exalt the LORD our God and worship at His holy mountain…" (Psalm 99:9). Verse 5 said to worship at His footstool, friends, and now the call is to worship at His holy mountain. The word that closes the call is mountain.
